primitives.name: Mixed-Rank Hero Vector
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Pre-match:** 113-dimensional tri-state hero vectors (xi = 1 Radiant, -1 Dire, 0 absent).
primitives.latex: \mathbf{x}_i = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if hero } i \text{ in Radiant} \\ -1 & \text{if hero } i \text{ in Dire} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
primitives.assumptions: Hero presence is binary and mutually exclusive between teams; pre-match team composition is static.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When hero pool is exhausted or team composition is invalid.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian belief update over player roles and team synergy states.
layer2.telemetry: Hero pick rate and win rate correlation.

primitives.name: Temporal Sliding Window Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **In-game:** 5-minute sliding-window time-series at the 20-minute mark (~half of an average 40-min game); 30 features per timestamp (team damage, kills, last hits, net worth, tower damage, XP) each as Dire, Radiant, R-D difference, and gradient; one model M_t trained per minute t = 4..n.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M_t': 'model at time t, dimensionless', 'X_{rt}': 'feature set at replay r, minute t, dimensionless', 'x_{i,t}': 'hero feature at time t, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Game state evolves smoothly; 20-minute mark is representative of mid-game dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When game duration exceeds 40 minutes or feature set becomes stale.

layer2.mapping: Derives GSE's live state transition kernel from temporal differentials of game metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of in-game win probability predictions at 20-minute mark.

These primitives form a dual system: static pre-match vectors for initial bias, and dynamic in-game models for refinement.
